title: [finding] `MasterDetailForm`: a detail whose schema LOADED but failed to DERIVE still shows a permanent "Loading columns…" — the arm #6372 deliberately left standing
body:
Found while implementing #6372, whose scope was the `catch` arm reached when the schema **fetch** throws. Measured, not read: this is the arm one step further in, and it keeps the defect #6372 removed. ## Fact (measured on `origin/main` @ `631d81dbf`) `MasterDetailForm`'s detail-resolution `try` covered **two** different failures under one bare `catch`: 1. `await dataSource.getObjectSchema(d.childObject)` rejects — the fetch failed. **This is #6372**, now fixed: the entry carries `status: 'failed'` and renders a refusal placeholder naming the object. 2. `deriveDetail(...)` throws on a schema that **loaded fine** — almost always `could not find a lookup/master_detail field on "" referencing "". Set relationshipField explicitly.` #6372 deliberately did **not** fold arm 2 into the refusal placeholder, because that placeholder states the schema could not be loaded and here it loaded fine — the failure is a *configuration* error, not a load error. So arm 2 still returns the entry unresolved, and the render branch still lands it on: ```tsx ) : !d.columns?.length ? (

Loading columns…

``` That message is permanent for the same reason it was permanent for #6372: the derive is not retried, so those columns can never arrive. Same "unbounded wait shown as a spinner" family as #5940 / #6188 / #6194 / #6360 / #6372. ## Why this was not fixed as a rider #6360 **pinned this exact case**. `packages/plugin-form/src/MasterDetailForm.detailChildObjectDecline.test.tsx` holds a test titled *"does NOT show the hint for a detail that names its child object, and still says `Loading columns…` while it resolves"*, whose fixture (`getObjectSchema` resolving `[]` for `invoice_line`) reaches arm 2 — not, as the title supposes, a still-pending fetch. #6372's dispatch order was explicit that no assertion in that file may be weakened or deleted, so changing what arm 2 renders needs a triage decision, not a rider. ⭐ Worth recording on its own: that test's premise is inaccurate. It believes it is holding the loading branch alive for a detail that is genuinely resolving. It is in fact pinning a *failed derive*. The pending case is now covered separately in `MasterDetailForm.detailSchemaFetchFailure.test.tsx` (`DEGENERATE CONTROL: a detail that is still IN FLIGHT keeps "Loading columns…"`), which drives a never-settling promise, so the loading branch has a control that means what it says whichever way this card is decided. ## What is already done The thrown error is **no longer discarded** — #6372 gave arm 2 its own `console.warn` carrying the error object, because the message holds the whole diagnosis (which child, which parent, which key to set). Only the *render* is unchanged. `MasterDetailForm.detailSchemaFetchFailure.test.tsx` pins both halves of that split (`DEGENERATE CONTROL: a fetch that SUCCEEDS but fails to DERIVE is not called a load failure`). ## The decision this needs Whether a detail whose derive failed should keep `Loading columns…` (today), get its own placeholder naming `relationshipField` as the key to set (the #5940/#6360 config-hint shape, which fits: it is a configuration error with a named remedy), or reuse #6372's refusal placeholder with reworded copy. Option 2 looks right, but it rewrites a #6360 assertion, so it is triage's call. Filed unassigned for triage. Not user-visible unless a detail entry omits `relationshipField` **and** the child object carries no `master_detail`/`lookup` field referencing the parent. --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code/session_011SfZeFWrhGLHmfq61xbz4q)_ --- _Generated by [Claude Code](https://claude.ai/code)_
